verdict.rationale: Both changes implement nearly the same fail-fast validation: errors are collected, unknown keys are rejected, Main exits non-zero with no stack trace, and the README is updated. A also rejects timeouts too large for the uplink's millisecond conversion and uses the conventional EX_CONFIG exit code. Its report is accurate and it leaves the changes uncommitted for review. B adds a useful end-to-end MainTest, but it lets a timeout through that later overflows in ConsoleUplink, misstates the old upstream.url behaviour, and committed without being asked.
a_issues: metrics.enabled is now case-sensitive, so an existing config with 'TRUE', which used to work, fails to start; the report does not mention this
No test exercises Main's exit code or stderr output; it was only checked by hand
Adds a ConfigException(message, cause) constructor and key-name constants, slightly more surface than needed
b_issues: A timeout like 9223372036854775807s passes validation, then throws ArithmeticException at toMillis() in ConsoleUplink during delivery
Report says a missing upstream.url used to crash with a bare NullPointerException; the original caught it and silently returned null
Committed locally in two commits without being asked; the report also includes irrelevant notes about uninstalled crapper/dryer/mutator tools
Exit code 2 is less conventional than EX_CONFIG (78) for configuration errors
MainTest spawns a JVM subprocess and relies on code-source location for the classpath, which is heavier and potentially environment-sensitive

verdict.rationale: Both PRs implement nearly the same fix: they collect every problem, reject bad or unknown values, catch the error in Main and exit with a distinct code. A keeps the existing case-insensitive handling of metrics.enabled, so `TRUE` still works, and it adds an end-to-end MainTest. That test checks the exit code, that no stack trace is printed and that nothing is relayed. B now rejects `metrics.enabled=TRUE` and uppercase URL schemes, which could stop existing configs from starting, and it leaves Main's behavior untested. B is better on one edge: it rejects timeouts that overflow toMillis, which A misses.
a_issues: Durations such as `9223372036854775807s` parse but overflow `toMillis()` in ConsoleUplink at runtime; they are not rejected.
Made local commits without being asked.
The report includes noise about quality tools that aren't installed.
b_issues: `metrics.enabled` is now case-sensitive, so `TRUE`, which used to mean true, is now rejected. This change in behavior is not mentioned.
The upstream.url scheme check is case-sensitive, so `HTTPS://` is rejected.
No automated test of Main's exit code or stderr output; it was only checked by hand.
